articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine I built Ghost in the Machine, a spooky interactive terminal where a mysterious digital ghost responds t…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built I built Ghost in the Machine , a spooky interactive terminal where a mysterious digital ghost responds to the user using a locally running open-weight AI model . The project is intentionally small and is built using only: HTML CSS JavaScript Ollama A local open-weight AI model Users can type commands or ask the ghost questions directly from the terminal. For example: visitor@ghost:~$ hello ghost The message is sent to the local AI model, which generates a response in the personality of the Ghost. I interpreted the theme as the idea of a computer that feels alive because something inside the machine can actually talk back. Demo Live Demo: Coming soon.

articles.title: Multi-Tenancy: What Changes When One Application Serves Many Organizations
articles.excerpt: "Design multi-tenant applications with deliberate data isolation, trusted tenant context, tenant-aware authorization, and boundary testing." Building software for one organization is different from bu…
articles.body: "Design multi-tenant applications with deliberate data isolation, trusted tenant context, tenant-aware authorization, and boundary testing." Building software for one organization is different from building software that serves many organizations. This distinction has become particularly relevant to me through work around school-management software. When an application serves a single organization, many assumptions can remain implicit. Users belong to the same organizational environment. Configuration is relatively straightforward. Data access often assumes a single administrative boundary. Those assumptions become dangerous when the same application serves multiple organizations.

articles.title: Business Name vs Domain Name vs Trademark: Three Different Things
articles.excerpt: Business Name vs Domain Name vs Trademark: Three Different Things Founders often use three phrases as if they meant the same thing: "I registered my business name," "I own the domain," and "I trademar…
articles.body: Business Name vs Domain Name vs Trademark: Three Different Things Founders often use three phrases as if they meant the same thing: "I registered my business name," "I own the domain," and "I trademarked it." They are three separate systems, owned by different authorities, and winning in one does not give you rights in the others. Confusing them is one of the most common and most expensive mistakes a new business can make. Here is how they actually differ, and what to check before you launch. 1. The business name: permission to trade A business name is the name under which you legally operate. In Pakistan, that usually means registering with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) for a company, or registering a firm or sole proprietorship under the relevant local law.
articles.author: Waseem Riaz

articles.title: Claude Code and Codex as agents on your team
articles.excerpt: A general AI agent with a shell can edit code. It is not very good at it. Coding agents like Claude Code and Codex are much better, because that is the only thing they are built to do: read a reposito…
articles.body: A general AI agent with a shell can edit code. It is not very good at it. Coding agents like Claude Code and Codex are much better, because that is the only thing they are built to do: read a repository, plan, edit, run the checks, fix, repeat. So instead of teaching every agent to code, we let them hand the code to a coding agent. This article explains how that works in AgenticOS, the open-source system for company agents we build at Vstorm, what it needs, and what a real task looked like. Drafted with AI assistance, edited and verified by the author. The idea in one paragraph In AgenticOS an agent is something your team builds in the browser: instructions, a model, knowledge and a set of tools it may use. The coding agent is one of those tools.
articles.author: Kacper Włodarczyk

articles.title: What I learned building wfreq
articles.excerpt: TL;DR How a word-frequency tool taught me to wrap errors instead of replacing them: from .expect() to thiserror, #[source] and per-file warnings. I built wfreq, a small Rust CLI that prints the most c…
articles.body: TL;DR How a word-frequency tool taught me to wrap errors instead of replacing them: from .expect() to thiserror, #[source] and per-file warnings. I built wfreq , a small Rust CLI that prints the most common words in .txt , .md , .pdf and .docx files. The counting took an afternoon. The error messages took the rest of the project. This post is about the hardest part: making the tool tell the truth when something goes wrong. Version 1: .expect() and a crash The first main read the file like this: let content = std :: fs :: read_to_string ( & args .file ) .expect ( "File can not read" ); I pointed it at a PDF and got: thread 'main' panicked at src/main.rs:30:57: File can not read: Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" } Two problems.
articles.author: Yash Kumar Saini

articles.title: Google-Extended isn't a crawler. Why our fetcher honours it anyway
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: we're Hybrid Forge Lab and we built Distill, the URL-to-Markdown API in this post. There's a free plan and a no-signup demo, so you can check everything below yourself. Google-Extended sho…
articles.body: Disclosure: we're Hybrid Forge Lab and we built Distill, the URL-to-Markdown API in this post. There's a free plan and a no-signup demo, so you can check everything below yourself. Google-Extended shows up in robots.txt like any other user agent: User-agent: Google-Extended Disallow: / But no bot ever sends it. Googlebot keeps fetching the page as before. The token only tells Google whether the content may be used for Gemini. Applebot-Extended does the same for Apple. So a fetcher that announces itself as DistillBot could skip that group and be technically right: it isn't Google-Extended. We don't skip it. Here's why, with numbers.

articles.title: A 4-step late-invoice follow-up sequence freelancers can copy (no awkward emails)
articles.excerpt: Late invoices are rarely about bad clients. Most of the time the invoice is sitting in someone's inbox, waiting for an approval nobody asked for. A clear, polite, scheduled follow-up fixes most of it.…
articles.body: Late invoices are rarely about bad clients. Most of the time the invoice is sitting in someone's inbox, waiting for an approval nobody asked for. A clear, polite, scheduled follow-up fixes most of it. Here's the sequence I use. Before you send the invoice Put the due date and payment method in the email body, not just the PDF. Name the person who approves payment. If you don't know, ask: "Who should I copy so this gets to accounts payable?" Use a specific subject line: Invoice #1042 – March design work – due Apr 15 . Step 1: Friendly reminder (3 days before due) Hi Sam, quick heads-up that invoice #1042 ($1,200) is due on Friday. The pay link is here: [link]. Thanks again for a great project! Step 2: Due-date nudge (1 day after due) Hi Sam, invoice #1042 was due yesterday.

articles.title: 26 Years Later, BioWare’s Most Influential RPG Is Still Shaping My Life
articles.excerpt: BioWare may be gone, but the studio's best RPG, Baldur's Gate 2, built a legacy that is still shaping lives today.
articles.body: The game was Baldur’s Gate 2: Shadows of Amn . The T-shirt, which came with the collector’s edition, sported the game’s logo: two mirrored heads, one in light, one in darkness (the exact meaning of the image has been debated for the past 26 years, with no conclusive answer). I was the kid, of course. Soon after, I bought the game and, for the first time, immersed myself in the world of the Forgotten Realms, brought to life in digital form by BioWare. Almost three decades later, BioWare is gone . The sad news made me reflect on how Baldur’s Gate 2 and the other computer RPGs they developed between the 1990s and the early 2000s marked the trajectory of my life.

articles.body: The powerful Vera Rubin Observatory has spotted what seems to be a dwarf planet circling the sun in the frigid depths beyond Neptune. The icy object, known as 2026 ED138, is likely between 600 and 1500 kilometers (373 to 972 miles) wide, scientists say. It's therefore probably big enough to be sculpted into a sphere by its own gravity — a key characteristic that separates dwarf planets from asteroids and other small space rocks. And if 2026 ED138 is indeed a dwarf planet, that's a pretty big deal, as astronomers have confirmed just five of them to date: Pluto , Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake . articles.title: Black holes can split in two — but only if they spin at extreme speeds
articles.excerpt: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. New research suggests that the opposite may happen too: single black holes may split in tw…
articles.body: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. These events are so violent that they set the very fabric of space ringing with ripples called gravitational waves. Now, new research suggests that the opposite may happen, too: single black holes may be able to split in two. But this can only happen if that progenitor black hole is spinning at maximum possible speed. That speed prevents the black holes from immediately falling back on each other. There are physical laws in place that would usually prevent black holes from splitting in two; the team behind this research investigated whether there are conditions in which these laws can be temporarily bypassed.
